saints.name: St. Richard the Pilgrim
saints.title: Pilgrim
saints.shortBlurb: An Anglo-Saxon father of saints who died on pilgrimage to Rome, and whose children carried the Gospel into Germany…
biography: Richard was a West Saxon of noble rank, remembered above all as the father of Willibald, Winnibald, and Walburga, all saints, and as a kinsman of Boniface, the apostle of Germany. About the year 720, leaving Walburga in the care of the abbess of Wimborne, he set out with his two sons on pilgrimage to Rome, embarking at Hamble-haven in Hampshire and crossing to Normandy.

At Lucca in Tuscany he fell sick and died, about the year 722, and his children buried him in the church of San Frediano, where his tomb became a place of veneration and miracles. The story of the family was written down by the nun Hugeburc of Heidenheim from Willibald's own telling.

The sons went on to Rome, and all three children later laboured with Boniface in the conversion of Germany — Willibald as bishop of Eichstätt, Winnibald as abbot of Heidenheim, and Walburga as abbess. The royal title that later legend gave their father is not borne out by history.
saints.knownFor: Fathering the missionary saints Willibald, Winnibald, and Walburga.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 7 February
